question:
(i) Explain the significance of the Davisson and Germer experiment.
(ii) Explain why atomic spectra and electron diffraction both indicate that classical ideas alone are not sufficient for microscopic systems.

options.A:
(i) Davisson-Germer experiment proved electrons behave only as particles.
(ii) Atomic spectra and electron diffraction are fully explained by classical ideas alone.
options.B:
(i) Davisson-Germer experiment verified the wave nature of photons, not electrons.
(ii) Atomic spectra are continuous and electron diffraction is impossible.
options.C:
(i) Davisson-Germer experiment showed diffraction maxima for electrons scattered by nickel, verifying de Broglie matter waves, $\lambda=\dfrac{h}{p}$.
(ii) Atomic line spectra require quantised levels, while electron diffraction requires matter waves; both show classical physics alone is insufficient.
options.D:
(i) The experiment verified $\lambda=hp$ for electrons.
(ii) Atomic spectra arise from continuous electron energies.
